facts.claim: Edinburgh Visitor Levy: 5% of the cost of paid overnight accommodation (accommodation-only portion, net of VAT), charged on the first 5 consecutive nights only, for stays from 24 July 2026, at the same rate every day of the year; applies to hotels, B&Bs, guest houses, hostels, aparthotels, self-catering and short-term lets, caravan/camp sites; not charged on extras like parking, meals, drinks or transport; the council called it Scotland's first visitor levy.

facts.claim: The council's provider guide (v2.1, Sept 2026) quotes the 2026 VisitScotland Guidance: the levy should be included as turnover and, if the provider is VAT-registered, is liable for VAT; the levy applies to providers below the VAT threshold too. So at a VAT-registered hotel the levy plus its VAT equals 5% of the VAT-inclusive room price (editorial arithmetic: £180 incl. VAT -> £150 net -> £7.50 levy + £1.50 VAT = £9/night; £27 for 3 nights; £45 for a 7-night stay).

sources.title: City of Edinburgh Council: Edinburgh Visitor Levy Scheme, information for accommodation providers, v2.1 Sept 2026 (PDF)

facts.claim: Stays on/after 24 July 2026 booked and paid for (in part or full) before 1 October 2025 are not subject to the levy; such bookings must specify specific dates, a precise number of rooms and a stated room price per night, and the payment must be tangible, attributable to a room and non-refundable (not refundable deposits). Stays that commenced before 24 July 2026 are not liable even if they finish after it.
